hook: Our children **won't look after us.** Is there a law?

slides.title: Yes, children **must** maintain parents.
slides.body: A parent or grandparent who can't maintain themselves from their own earnings or property can claim maintenance from adult children or grandchildren, so they can lead a normal life.

slides.title: No children? **Relatives** too.
slides.body: A childless senior citizen (60 or above) can claim from an adult relative with sufficient means who holds their property, or who would inherit it.

timeline.text: You apply, or if you can't, someone you authorise.
The Tribunal can order an **interim** monthly allowance.
Decided within 90 days of notice; extendable once, by up to 30 days.

slides.title: How much? Up to **₹10,000** a month.
slides.body: Your State sets the maximum monthly allowance, but it cannot exceed ₹10,000. If it isn't paid, the Tribunal can jail the defaulter up to one month per unpaid month, or until payment.

slides.title: Gave away property? It **can be undone.**
slides.body: If you gifted or transferred property after this Act, on condition they provide your basic needs, and they don't, the Tribunal can declare the transfer **void** at your option.

slides.title: Abandoning an elder is a **crime.**
slides.body: If someone who has the care or protection of a senior citizen leaves them anywhere, intending to wholly abandon them, it can mean up to 3 months' jail, a fine up to ₹5,000, or both. It's cognizable and bailable.

sources: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 – Sections 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 12, 16, 17, 23, 24, 25
caption:
Children refusing to support their elderly parents? The law is on the parents' side. 👇

1️⃣ Parents and grandparents who can't maintain themselves can claim maintenance from adult children and grandchildren
2️⃣ Maintenance covers food, clothing, residence and medical treatment
3️⃣ Apply to the Maintenance Tribunal; it should decide within 90 days of notice, and can order interim maintenance meanwhile
4️⃣ The State sets the maximum, which cannot exceed ₹10,000 a month
5️⃣ Property given on condition of care can be declared void if the care stops
6️⃣ Abandoning a senior citizen in your care can mean up to 3 months' jail, a ₹5,000 fine, or both
⚠️ Parents can also claim under BNSS Sec 144, but not under both laws. Appeal against a Tribunal order within 60 days

Source: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 (Sec 2, 4, 5, 9, 12, 16, 23, 24); Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Sec 144)
